We were generally happy with our trip as planned to Costa Rica but it was not as exceptional as I had hoped.  Upon arrival in San Jose we were supposed to be met by someone from Jacada with a Jacada sign with our name.  There are dozens of people waiting outside of arrival so it is a bit hectic, but our driver was not there when we arrived and it took perhaps 15-30 minutes to track him down.  Hotel in San Jose was very nice and a good selection.  Driver the next morning was on time and got us to our short plane flight to Puerto Jimenez which went fine.  Arrival in Puerto Jimenez was fine and we were greeted by Lapa Rios staff who were all outstanding.  Lapa Rios was the highlight of our trip.  Room was wonderful, staff were great, tours were fun.  Transfer back to Puerto Jimenez was fine.  Upon arrival back at San Jose we were once again waiting for driver to take us to El Silencio.  It was a short wait and the driver was very nice.  El Silencio is a nice lodge and we had excellent accommodations (although some maintenance issues with the room).  What we did not realize was how far it was from everything else we were doing.  The next day was a drive to the Arenal Hanging Bridges.  Holy crap it was over 2 hours away!  Why did they recommend a hotel that was so far from what we wanted to do?  The driver was nice and stopped and showed us some wildlife along the way.  After the hanging bridges we were supposed to do a volcano walk.  Unfortunately our driver had no idea what our itinerary was supposed to be and we had to try and call to figure out what we were supposed to do.  In the end we did a short hike at the volcano that was unimpressive.  The next day was zip lining and white water rafting.  It would have helped if Jacada had told us the name of the company we were doing this with.  A driver arrived who did not speak English and took us on an hour or so drive at break neck speed. The zip line and rafting guides from Pozo Azul were all very nice and we had a nice lunch as well.  Once again the same driver took us home and was probably the most death defying part of the day.  Transfer from El Silencio to the Guanacaste coast was fine, another long, four hour plus!, drive. Again the driver was nice, stopped for some food and a little site seeing along the way. We arrived at El Mangroove which was a nice hotel unfortunately, by this point the pandemic of Covid-19 was taking over everything.  The hotel was nearly vacant and our flight home was cancelled.  So after just one night at the hotel we decided we needed to beat it out of Costa Rica before they shut everything down.  In the end we had to cut our trip short by three days (of course this is not Jacada's fault). Last move was to call Jacada to have them rearrange our transport from the hotel back to the airport which they did but were all too fast to remind me that my hotel rooms were non-refundable.  So as noted, average.

I had my initial visit to this clinic 5 years ago and was overwhelmed by the service, following which I left a good review and showed my gratitude to the staff with gifts. I recently returned to their new clinic and this review is to supersede my previous one, which was mis-informed at the time, to express my disappointment with the after service and hopefully give a true representation of what to expect form Dental Center Antalya.Both myself and my partner had the same package with the lifetime warranty and aftercare that this center boasts about.  5 years later, in an attempt to make use of this after care, we booked flights to Turkey for a follow up treatment. Upon arriving to their new clinic, the service and personal attention we had received from our first trip was not matched, making the experience as a whole uncomfortable. Over 5 years, there has been a clear decline in the level of customer service. Although their new premises consist of complimentary drinks from their café, this compromise does not justify the lower standard of care when compared to their clinic in 2015.The reason for our trip was for a checkup following an x-ray done on my teeth in the UK, where my dentist had advised that I should go back to Dental Center Antalya. My partner also had gaps coming through and a crack in one of her crowns. While they were happy to rectify the issues with my partners teeth (replacing front teeth, canine to canine), my personal after service was appalling. They refused to honor their lifetime guarantee, and had given me a quote, even though they had agreed to cover my partners teeth under the same guarantee. When I raised my concerns, they could not justify to me why they could not apply the same service to me as they did with my partner. From sheer frustration, I booked a flight back on the same day, losing out on the money spent for the trip and 5-star hotel.Having returned, I have since received a quote from a Harley Street dental clinic for £6000 to cover the same works and lifetime guarantee. Although this is more expensive, I hope that this review would help advise people in a similar position to myself that this option is cheaper and more convenient in the long run. It saves multiple week-long trips to Turkey which, all in all, would be around 2000 a time. If you are happy to stay in a 1-star hotel or bed and breakfast for the week, then this Dental Center Antalya might be more financial viable, however in light of the additional charges, and considering most people would not want to spend a week in uncomfortable accommodation, a UK clinic would prove more appropriate and convenient. I am not one to go out of my way to write negative reviews, but the purpose of this is to give anyone considering treatment in Turkey an insight into what it entails, and the frustrations you are likely to face, in order to allow you to make a more accurate comparison with any other options you might be considering. Lastly, I would kindly ask Dental Center Antalya to remove my picture from their website as soon as possible, along with my previous review as it does not accurately reflect the current service of the centre.Simon Faherty

I asked them to prioritise the health of my teeth and I wanted options to make them look better. The initial suggestion was 8-10 crowns on my top and 8-10 on my bottom teeth, which I found very strange as my bottom teeth are perfectly healthy. I had to ask for less invasive options, which should have been initially discussed. Not everyone wants a ‘Hollywood Smile’.  Also, there was no enthusiasm from the staff. However, I was happy with the final plan as it was more reasonable. The coordinator answered my questions to a satisfactory degree.Root Canal Treatment: 2/5The initial consultation was followed by my root canal treatment (same day). The root canal procedure was terrible. I will be clear and say that I was not in pain during or after the procedure. However, it was extremely uncomfortable and overwhelming. 1) The dentist did not warn me that he will inject anaesthetics - this surprised me and I couldn’t do anything as the needle was already in my gum.  2) He was very rough in his approach - I know this is an invasive procedure, but at least TRY to be gentle and empathetic when handling my mouth. He did not show any care. I actually developed a small rash which I am certain is from the equipment that he was using as it was rubbing on to the side of my mouth causing a lot of friction (I sent them a photo of this). 3) I was not asked once if I was okay, my neck and jaw were very uncomfortable. The dentist did not speak English well so communicating was difficult, and communication is the most important thing in any treatment. Teeth Preparation: 5/5 This was so much better. It was with a different dentist who was reassuring, explained what he was going to do and communicated very well. The procedure was smooth. I asked him a few questions and he was very helpful. Crown fitting & Overall result: 5/5This was with the same dentist that prepared my teeth. He made some aesthetic adjustments to the crowns. Although the crowns do not completely match my natural teeth, I was expecting this as I have some discolouration in my natural teeth. It definitely looks a lot better than before the treatment which I am happy about. Final thoughts:I am not the only one to make a complaint of this nature. It is clear that they are seeing so many patients which makes the process feel scripted and lack enthusiasm, personalised care and empathy. Customer satisfaction involves the process and results. The results are good, but in my case, DCT neglected the process - which was terrible. There are inconsistencies in their overall care so I would not recommend this clinic.Edit: DCT initially attempted to remove this review and they flagged it as ‘Fake’ even though I had a full discussion about my experience with the operations manager prior to posting this. I have now verified my experience with trust pilot so it was posted. Due to the dishonesty, I’ve reduced the rating from 3 to 2 stars.

People use this service as a last resort before unmonitored self medication. Once a genuinely life-saving provider, they have now coasted on their existing goodwill to erode everything that once made this service worthwhile. There is a recurring membership fee on top of all other fees, and yet somehow I need to tell them my medical history every time I talk to them. It feels like they put all the work onto the patient, to the point that it's hard to believe that they even keep records of their own. When they inevitably mess something up, or if your situation has changed in a way they don't expect in advance, everything is an automated no-reply email address or AI chatbot and there's no recourse. Or you can talk to someone on the phone for £7.50 with no guarantee that they're allowed to fix your problem. They've added extra prescriber fees recently despite the process becoming more automated and less reliable and despite charging a monthly fee on top of that.The service has declined sharply since I started with them some 4 years ago, and even back then it was seen as a bit of a last resort option for the desperate.Right now, they are the bottom of the barrel, and they know that, and they're doing all they can to provide the laziest service possible at the highest price they can, knowing that the rest of the trans healthcare system is so messed up that people have no choice but to use them anyway.I write this review on the back of having had my hormone dosage suddenly halved for the next 3 months, after years of stability, as a punishment for late blood test results. No short term emergency prescription to give time to fix things, no reminder, no indication that anything was wrong until the prescription itself came through. And of course, they now charge you through the nose to automatically generate the letter to the GP saying you need blood tests done. (Of course they make you fill out a form saying what blood tests you need, because apparently even filling that themselves is too much effort for them.) This is expensive and humiliating and abusive but what choice do I have? And they know most of us don't have any other choice, so they're never going to get better.Update 2025-Jan-03: They have tried to pull the same thing on me again. I've been double charged for this prescription so far and they've given me three: one with a halved dose, and two with no estrogen at all. I am fairly certain now that they do not retain a record of blood test results, which further calls into question what I'm paying the subscription fee for. The only thing stopping me from doing what GenderGP does myself is that my signature does not hold the same weight at the pharmacy.

(Update)-------------------------------------------------------------Quickly after raising my concerns, Airpets contacted me. As the reply to that review, they do not have control over which cargo company handle the pets once at destination, the airline companies do. So, British Airways was the airline company my pets flew with, and they use Mercury Cargo.For information, the Mercury Cargo warehouse is also IAG Cargo so if the airline company you use work with them, your pets will be handle like freight shipments not live animals. -------------------------------------------------------------(Previous review below)I shipped my pets with Airpets from London to Los Angeles. While they are very nice and professional people (friendly when I dropped my cats, offered me to send me updates through WhatsApp), nobody mentioned how pets are handled at Mercury Cargo (company they work with at destination, LAX). So, I did come at 1930 to get my paperwork, and they told me to come back at 2100 as it was not ready. Additionally, no one explained to me that I had to sign up to "get in line". The pets are NOT kept in a climate controlled room and they are left on wooden palettes in the middle of forklift machine moving freight around, in a freight warehouse not an live animal allocated room.The great reputation Airpets has might be because they often take care of the entire trip, which means pets owners get their pets at their door and so they don't see this. My cats peed themselves (which did not happened on longer trip in the past) and were in shock to have been handled the way they were handled, plus they were waiting next to crates with barking dogs (I understand that the dogs barked, I love dogs. They were crying as they saw their owners waiting). Why would Airpets people be so amazing and do such a great job at departure to then allow such situation at destination? I do not understand.

Firstly, I wanted to praise the staff. Not only were they friendly and very efficient, they also managed to keep a straight face when they brought out the food.Now, I know the Hungry Horse is the Ryanair of hospitality, and I was not expecting fine dining, but I did expect the food to be edible.I now know why it’s called the Hungry Horse. It’s because the horse would never go near the offerings, in this case from the festive menu (which incidentally was about as festive as my big toe).To add insult to injury we had a French man in our party who prides himself on his culinary abilities. Tragically he order the Brie and Cranberry bites as a starter. No salad as advertised. Just three sad little deep fried triangles slung on a plate with some cranberry sauce.The rest of the starters were acceptable - the soup, prawn cocktail and chicken strips were fine.Unfortunately, this was followed by the main course. The vegan members of our group were given Yorkshire puddings with their roast. In any ither situation this would have been a bonus because the remaining guests would have gladly fought over a spare yorky. Alas ladies and gents, this is no Toby. They tasted like a combination of wallpaper paste and flour, cooked in a hot oven for 30 minutes then kicked along a pavement before landing on your plate. The vegetables were so overcooked that it looked like a pile of slop and had zero flavour. The roast potatoes were OK.The Brussels sprouts with cheese was not cooked so I am not sure how it was ‘crisped under the grill’ . It had to go back but looked so revolting on its return we did not eat it.The absolute piece de resistance was the ‘turkey’. Never in my life have I been presented with such an abomination. I can genuinely say the slices of heavily processed poultry tasted, I kid you not, like you were eating the contents of a pig pen. I have no idea what was in it but Bernard Matthew’s would turn in his grave.Desserts were largely fine although my husband’s Christmas pudding would definitely be classed as a slither in our house.The warning signs were there. The restaurant was virtually empty, the bar service was slow and they were very short staffed.Either that or they were all running about catching the tumbleweed.I will sum this up and say that my husband never ever complains. He was going to speak to the staff on the way out because he was so astounded we could be charged for food that I would not offer as a booby prize to someone detained at His Majesty’s Pleasure.Being terribly British, and knowing that this sub par fayre is not the fault of the chap in charge of the microwave, we paid up and left.But Greene King, when the fat cats are sitting around the board table soon, planning Christmas 2025, desperately trying to increase profits, get them to mystery shop NOW so they have a chance to see what you are serving up.Yes, it was £20 a head. Yes, generally in life you get what you pay for, but it has to be palatable don’t you think?Greene King, Christmas is about making memories and this is something we as a family will never forget. So thank you for that.

All members of this chain thought the transfer was free!This is what Smarttrace have to say: Implant Fees: These fees typically range from £25-£35 and are paid directly to the veterinarian or implanter. This covers the microchip itself, the insertion procedure, and often a basic consultation. Breeders are responsible for microchipping their litters before selling, but these costs do not include registering the pet with an owner. In short, this is the payment for the product and the labour of implanting the product. Registration Fees: This is where pet owners come in. After acquiring a microchipped pet, you'll need to register your contact information with a microchip database. Veterinary clinics may offer free registration on their internal system, but these often have limitations. I can only write a partial review of Audley because I never got past the planning and pricing part.My initial experience with Audley was very positive, thanks to their outstanding travel consultant Alex. Alex is Audley's Spain and Portugal expert and in all my communications with her, both by email and on the phone she was upbeat, helpful and seemingly enthusiastic about customizing the tour to meet every one of our trip wishes. I will have to admit that the final customized tour she created for us was outstanding. The problem came with the price. Now I understand there is a premium to be paid for a customized tour. As with any other company, Audley has an organizational overhead and needs to make a profit. However, when that profit is more than 36% over the actual cost of the tour, I think that is excessive.   I know how much over the actual price of the tour Audley was charging because I priced the itinerary they provided independently, looking up the costs of the hotels and private tours identical to the ones that they described in their itinerary. In fact, I made sure that I rounded everything way up to make sure I gave them the benefit of the doubt. Even doing that, a trip that I could have booked on my own with just a bit of effort for $7,200 was costing me over $11,300 with Audley. Sure, we will be taking a cab rather than a private car from the train station to the hotel and back but for $4,100 less, I can certainly live with that. To make matters worse, the international flight from the US to Spain that Alex told me should could probably get me at a cheaper price through Audley contracts with the airlines, ended up being over $900 more expensive than the same flights I was able to find online in less than 10 minutes.   If you don't mind the  unnecessary personal extravagance of blowing a couple of thousand dollars for customized service then I guess Audley is for you.  I'd rather save that money and take another trip.****Addendum 10/09/2022As Audley Travel promised in their reply to my original post, a customer service manager, Lily, did reach out to me shortly afterwards to discuss my concerns. Once again, as in my experience with Alex,  my original Audley trip consultant, Lily was  extremely pleasant, patient and apparently very determined to explain the value of the Audley tour and try to work with me in any way to get the trip with them off the ground. Despite the effort, we could not arrive at a solution that would allow me to feel comfortable with the value I was getting for my money. Just as a matter of perspective,  by creating and booking an itinerary on my own, totally online, with a virtually identical itinerary to Audley's with the same hotels plus full day as opposed to the 1/2 day tours offered by Audley in all the places we planned to visit, I saved enough to pay for our two roundtrip flight fares from the U.S. to Spain in premium economy class.  In the final analysis, I was extremely impressed with the patience and apparent determination the Audley team has in creating a great trip for it's clients. Unfortunately for me, the steep premium that involves just does not make financial sense.

In spring of 2022 the Kraken user interface (UI) showed a lower margin level (%) than it should be. The margin level is important as it is preferred to stay above 100%. At < 100% you're is not able to open new spot positions on margin. At 40% or lower Kraken may liquidate your positions.According to Kraken it was experiencing a visual bug where the EUR/USD rate on the web UI was quoting a rate of 1.21. Due to this, users holding a EUR balance as collateral were experiencing a visual bug where they saw a higher equity, free margin and margin level.As far as we know, Kraken did not release a post regarding (the existence and resolution of) this bug.Did you also expercienced this bug, or are you still experiencing it? Check it by calculating your margin level (yML).To calculate your margin level (yML) you need to know your trade balance (TB), current valuation (CV), opening cost (OC) and leverage (L):  yML = (TB+(CV-OC))/(OC/L)*100.Compare your margin level (yML) with the margin level on your Kraken user interface and give us your feedback.PON

We then checked into our hotel and it was very nice, comfy beds and lovely food down in the restaurant too. The next morning, we got picked up on time for the hospital and I ended up having my surgery early morning so was out of theatre by midday. When I was taken down, so many staff members were in their scrubs but on their phones which did worry me. Before the surgery however, just after my payment, the translator just left the hotel. So, there was then a major language barrier and the nurses didn't really seem to bother with me beyond the basic administered medication timings to the point that they actually forgot one of my pain medication doses for hours until my companion had to go through to tell them, at which point a nurse ran through with a fast acting tablet. When one of the nurses came in to do my observations, she was chatting to someone the whole time on her phone. On the day of discharge, we were told to be ready for 8am and the driver didn't show up until 10.20am. I was given a prescription I couldn't read as it was obviously in Turkish and taken to a pharmacy to pay for my medication. At no point was I told what each medication was for and told how often to take it (Google helped with that one). When I went back for my final check up there was another lady from my hotel who'd had the same procedure yet we were prescribed slightly different additional medicines and told different aftercare rules. On our final morning, the driver was 20 minutes late taking us to the airport so we genuinely thought we'd have to get a taxi. Now I have come home I have been assigned an aftercare co-ordinator, and they have been very responsive and helpful. I was sent basic aftercare instructions but none for my arm lift after the surgery, but my co-ordinator has been very good at getting responses for me quickly and providing me with what I ask for. The aftercare has been the best part of the experience with Clinic Center. Overall, I found Clinic Center's service to be really unorganised and unhelpful. My surgery however was a success and I am very happy with my results so far, my surgeon was very good and I am recovering well and will hopefully see the results soon. My aftercare co-ordinator has also been great, very helpful. However, the organisation of the whole experience by Clinic Center was a big let down.

I started my journey importing my dog to Australia in July 2022 when someone suggested using Sophie from AirPets to carry out the necessary steps for me.This, unfortunately, has not been my experience with AirPets. My dog is my world, like most, so for me importing him safely, happily and with a competent company was of the utmost importance. I trusted Sophie with the process and it has honestly caused me more stress, tears and anxiety than I can express. From the start, Sophie’s communication was lacking (she even commented on this herself, admitting that communication had been lacking) and there were several times where I was concerned about her management of my import request. The first issue was after our initial discussions when I had sent payment for the import permit with confirmation that the permit was being applied for, to receive an email the next day stating that she would need a copy of the RNATT test results to start the import application. I was pretty concerned at this point, but as Sophie had come recommended I decided to carry on.  (NB: the person that recommend AirPets initially is now no longer recommending AirPets and is instead using a different Agent). At every step of the process, I had to chase Sophie to get answers/results. Not once did she send over documentation without me chasing her for it, and this was always some time after she had received it! Even the Veterinary Schedule that you’re supposed to receive alongside your initial payment for the permit, I had to chase - explaining to Sophie that the lack of information was causing me some stress meant she sent over a tentative schedule with a single date on! It was just a constant hassle to get anything out of Sophie - the worst being the PEQ Booking & updated Import Permit - the PEQ Booking Number (PRN) was actually never sent to me (until the very end of our communication after multiple times asking for it), nor was the booking confirmed until I chased Sophie about the dates as I had been told that the date we requested was fully booked & the updated Import Permit, which I was told about on Oct 21st, was completed on November 1st and I didn’t get it until I emailed Sophie letting her know I was no longer going to be working with her on Nov 18th.I honestly thought the whole thing couldn’t get much worse, until I let Sophie know that I had lost faith in her ability to complete the import of my dog, to which her response was “thanks for the feedback, I’ll go ahead and cancel your quarantine spot”. To say that I was shocked at the response would be an understatement. It seemed like a very petty way to respond to someone, given how poor communication had been throughout. This then ensued a back and fourth of emailing for near 24hrs of me asking Sophie to provide the PRN Number for the booking (at this point, I honestly didn’t trust that the booking had been made, so at the very least I wanted the PRN as confirmation for the booking) with Sophie, as per usual, ignoring my requests and instead pressuring for payment (of £42 for the booking fee, which is a nice upcharge of over double given that the current cost for the PEQ fee is just over £15 - £27AUD).To say my experience with AirPets has been underwhelming would be an understatement and I would not recommend them to anyone. I would in fact, tell them to run the other way and avoid them. For a process that is beyond important for most pet owners, the way that Sophie handled things was just abysmal.

Over the past few months I have discovered some bugs in Krakens User Interface.One of the bugs concerns wrongly calculated Margin trade balance and hence wrong Margin level.This bug at Kraken let me to believe that my Margin trade balance, and my Margin level were higher than they were in reality. This is because the User Interface shows a higher Margin Trade Balance than the sum of my assets.  The sum of the assets must be the same as the Margin Trade Balance.However my user interface shows a Margin Trade Balance of 86.742,59 USD instead of 66.607,82 USD.Kraken’s interface shows a margin level of 136,85 % instead of the correct margin level of approx. 108%. This correct Margin Level is calculated according to krakens formulas;  ML = (TB+(CV-OC))/(OC/5)*100  (I can go into more depth about this if people are interested…)Assuming that Kraken uses the correct way to calculate Margin Level in their back log, this would mean my positions could be closer to liquidation level while my UI still shows healthy or less dangerous margin level. So in theory while the back log may have calculated a Margin Level of 40% or less (which will liquidate your position as this is the liquidation level), the UI may still have shown well above this threshold. This can negatively impact your decision making when it for example comes to adding more margin to your position or strategically liquidating your position before you hit critical levels.I wonder if Kraken did actually expose me, and other Kraken users, to an increased risk of being liquidated without our knowledge…

Show me the money! Clinical care without looking at the dog!We took my 9 year old Cockapoo to Willows veterinary centre with Canine immune-mediated thrombocytopenia (ITP). This is a common clinical disorder in which platelets are destroyed an auto immune disorder. When we arrived our dog was happy and wagging his tail, despite being already quite ill - he was happy as always. Upon initial examination and questions about his health and insurance it was decided to check his platelet levels, give him so treatment and we could take him home and continue caring for him.One hour later we were told his anaemia levels had also dropped so they had to admit him. (Not 100% sure I believe this now)Over the next 4 days we were sporadically updated on our dogs health, always referring to blood levels infrequently commenting on his general health. He was give a blood transfusion to help him. We were told we would be called, and we tried calling many times to get an update, but the calls were always later than promised or planned. We were not even called after his transfusion to tell us the success!Finally after 4 days I received a call to tell me his blood results were improving and we had "maxed out" on our insurance, so it was OK for us to collect him. They preferred to keep him one more day, but he was OK for collection. This was the first time money was spoken about since the first consultation. It was really obvious they didn't believe there was much money left in my dog, therefore it was OK to discharge him.When they brought our dog into the waiting area he almost didn't recognise us. It was clear to us they had ignored the general well being of the dog, they didn't care for the patient - they had the money!We were given medicines to give to our dog. The tablets came with a discharge letter - when the next dos was due and main side effects, but no instructions: what order should we give the tablets; with food or without; could we remove table from plastic pellet? So difficult to know. Surely some basic leaflets / instructions should have been provided?Overall I regret taking our dog to The Willows veterinary centre. He went in a happy dog and came out broken, but in their eyes healthy. There was not enough care or attention for the way the dog himself was responding to the treatment...just 100% focus on the clinical results and the money they could take.Four days later we said our sad and last goodbye to our best friend. I can not help reflect on the final days / week of his life. they would have been so much better at home being cared for.We had our dog treated at Fitzpatrick referral centre in 2019 - what a different experience. They showed so much care for the dog and gave some treatment free as it took us over our insurance yearly maximum. What a difference! If you are thinking about taking your pet here - my advice...think long and hard - I don't believe they care for the animal.

I found McCambridge Duffy to be efficient, helpful and non-judgemental. Things were quite straight forward all in all, and they were happy to answer any questions I had along the way.  Of course as with any company dealing in IVA's MCCambride Duffy will receive good money for their work, but the good news is for those applying for the IVA that this is not out of their pocket, but the creditors. AN amount is agreed upon between the creditors and McCambridge Duffy but your payments are not affected. I felt it was my best option, as with the amount I owed,and what I was paying each month was no longer viable. My payments have been cut in half now each month, and although an IVA lasts five years (unless I can pay more into it quicker) the end result is less money paid out by myself than if I had kept going the way I was with high interest loans. It is worth looking into for peace of mind and to stop juggling so many creditors (I had about 10 and was going a little crazy from the constant calls when I missed payments I could no longer afford) Glad I have done it now.

Update:I’m quite saddened to write this update really but feel it’s necessary for transparency. All started well with this company and I slowly moved my dogs diet over to Different Dog which went well over a period of time. All in all everything seemed good however I started to notice that my dogs stool started to go greener as the days went on. After a little while and observing that the green of the stool was what could be described as grass green all the way through and sometimes a darker blue bottle green I made contact with my vet who advised to withdraw from the food and make contact with Different Dog to understand if this was something they had heard of before and / or if there’s an ingredient that could cause this. On 17th February I made contact with Different Dog who to be fair were extremely helpful advising that red cabbage may cause this however out of the two recipes I had received only one had this ingredient. They offered a consultation with their nutritionalist who to this day besides me making further contact to chase has not made any effort to contact me. My dog is now on her previous diet and I have a quantity of different dog food in my freezer I cannot use. I feel it’s quite disappointing really that this company state that customers have access to a nutritionalist and vet however when needed this never materialises and poor that their customer satisfaction guarantee is not adhered to. I was quite excited that I had found a ‘healthy’ diet for my dog however now feel very dissatisfied and let down. .........................................I have been reviewing different dog food for a period of time now to change my miniature schnauzer’s diet. Different Dog is not as well known as some other brands but interested me as their recipes were all human grade, 60% protein and did not contain nasties. In addition I was impressed at the transparency of their recipes. The ordering and delivery process was fantastic. I received an email and text service to keep me up to date. And when delivered the packaging of the contents were as expected - well packaged and pleasing to the eye. The food itself smells lovely and you can see the different ingredients when spooning it out. Our dog loves her food and licked the bowl for a while afterwards. For us, we introduced the food too quickly and our little one did have an upset stomach. We reintroduced it a short time later slowly when her tummy had settled and she seems absolutely fine. I must add that the communication and customer service of the company is fantastic too. I have mailed and received mails back from Georgie quickly and I also telephoned and spent a while having all my questions answered by Steph. I have also been offered if needed a free of charge appointment over the telephone with their vet if required. I genuinely do not so far have anything negative to say about Different Dog. I wish more people knew about this company and the health benefits to their dogs from this food. A tip I can leave for others is that buy in larger volumes for cost effectiveness- for example, our little one needs 250g a day so we have ordered the 1000g packages. This will last her 4 days per pack and saved us just under £30 per month 🙂🙂 Overall, fantastic service and food 🥰🥰

However, the fluffy type of stuffing provided takes too much time to 'bed in' for a dog. If too little is left in, the bed serves no purpose, but too much and the bed entrance becomes limited, unstable and uninviting for the dogs to enter. Dogs do not like unstable conditions. The chaos only intensifies as you approach passport control, where you're likely to encounter significant wait times. I had to call the airline in the afternoon of the 5th day to ask if I actually have a reservation and why it was taking an agent so long to issue their E-tickets. They confirmed my reservation and said it is the agent's responsibility to issue the tickets, unless they have purchased from a consolidation. The airline explained that if my E-tickets were not issued, they would have to release the reservation. I expressed these concerns to Bob. He assured me that it is a 5 star airline and that it is safe. I asked why the change and he explained that the flight on the original airline company was overbooked. I asked for a discount on the new airline he wanted me to use for the inconvenience over the 5 days and he said to me that they are not charging me anymore money as the flight is quite expensive, but they are giving it to me at the price I paid for with the original airline. Bob sent me the provisional booking of this new airline to go through. I, then, recalled the original airline I booked with told me I had a reservation. I called Flight office again within 10mins of the first call. Luckily, it was Andrew that picked this time. I explained what his manager - Bob said. He initially supported him until I told him I had spoken to the original airline in the afternoon. This is when Andrew - the Flight Office agent now said to me they want me to fly with original (First) airline I paid for and he will do his best to get my E-tickets. At this point, I complained to Andrew that since the payment date above, I have not heard from him and it has been his colleagues (Daniel, Glen etc) dealing with my calls and telling me my ticket will be with me within 24hrs each day I called. I said to him it would have been nice to have a follow up call over this 5 day period and someone to tell me the truth exactly what was happening between them and the original airline I booked with. Andrew apologised and said he will get back to me 8pm that night of the 5th day. He called me back approximately 8.12pm and confirmed my E-tickets were out and I will get them by 4pm the next day - day 6. Day 6 - 28/11/2017 at 4pm I did not receive any e-mails of E-tickets from Andrew nor the Flight Office. I got worried again. I thought I wait till evening. After 13 months post hair transplant I am here to write a review.I don’t usually write reviews, but if I do is because something went really good or really wrong.In this case, and with great disappointment, I have to say that the outcome of the hair transplant went wrong.I had high expectations of the final results of the treatment considering all the reviews on here, but unfortunately it is totally different than expected.I am a woman, I was 28 years old at the time of my hair transplant procedure and I always had a full head of hair. My decision to undergo a hair transplant had been made because my hairline has always been too high and I wanted it to be a bit lower.The number of grafts transplanted and the density created in my new transplanted area was not matched considering my existing hair and its density, which resulted in a very poor and dissatisfying result.This was obvious straight after all the scabs came off, and by the time I was able to see the number of grafts transplanted. Spaces between grafts were too wide, and density created was poor. I could clearly see it was very different compared to my existing hair right above the transplanted area, but it was my first time undergoing a hair transplant so I trusted the process and hoped I was just being paranoid.Well, after over a year after the procedure I can totally say… I was right!Being a person who takes care of my appearance, the results of it really makes me sad.I look like someone who is actually suffering from hair loss, instead of the opposite, especially because it is right on the top of my forehead, so it is so easy and clear to see. You can see my scalp very well and it doesn’t look good at all.I believe the procedure hasn’t been done correctly, and in the most precise and best way possible, and this frustrates me so much. I expect people to care about delivering the best results, but I can’t say this was done in my case.I am so disappointed and words can’t describe my feelings about this.I am now forced to look for another professional who can fix this hair transplant on my head, and hopefully make me achieve the result I wanted.I followed the aftercare religiously and really looked after it.I gave 2 stars reviews only because I can’t fault the overall service provided.Everyone was very nice, and I didn’t encounter any problem in interacting and dealing with all the people involved in the whole process. They were really good and I had a great experience in Istanbul, so thank you so much for that!But, sadly, this doesn’t change the most important thing I came over there for: great final result.This is my own experience, and I am not here to recommend or not their services.Everyone has to make up their own minds, and make a choice for themselves. But, I have to be brutally honest and share my personal experience.

They also reviewed the scan images from Window to the Womb and expressed concern about the inaccurate measurements and the apparent lack of expertise. This misdiagnosis caused us immense, needless emotional trauma.When I raised these issues with the clinic, their response was dismissive and unprofessional. Ashley falsely claimed they had explained everything during the scan, but this was simply untrue.Since this experience, my wife and I remain more anxious and cautious than before. I decided to order the kit that I had seen many adverts for on social media. I suspected it might be a bit of con but thought I might as well be the guinea pig for my friendship group. I have now told all my friends to steer clear. I collected the blood sample and sent it off, and got the results 2-3 weeks later. The results immediately read that my AMH levels are "Out of range: High"- this immediately made me worried. The next page in the report goes into further details and shows my AMH level on a scale. It states normal is between 4.93 and 34.99. Mine is indicated as being 35.55 (0.56 higher than "normal" according to their scale).It then says directly below "This suggests you may have polycystic ovaries". A bold and worrying statement. I then decided google AMH levels to find out more, I'm glad I did because it turns out "normal" for someone aged between 20-29 is 13.1 - 53.8. Meaning my result sits well within the range of normal. The report then recommends a series of tests I should do to follow up given my worrying results , including but not limited to a pelvic ultrasound for the not so small price of £219. Hertility are taking advantage of the anxiety women have about their reproductive health to make money. Had I not done further research I might genuinely be concerned I have polycystic ovaries  (despite having none of the core symptoms). Since my terrible experience I read other reviews online where girls were told there numbers were worrying and as a result went to their GP's only to be retested and had completely different results. That being said I questions where any of the findings were even accurate in themselves, let alone the analysis of the data. Playing on peoples anxieties is so sick and twisted and can leave women feeling stressed and worried- avoid and don't fall into their trap, if you are worried about any aspect of your physical health go to the GP, in a way I'm glad I didn't so that I could learn about this and warn others.

I then went to another room to begin the preparation process and it was an entirely different oral surgeon and somebody I’ve never seen before, which was weird. Also when we did the prep work and I was numbed, they hit a nerve that you should be trained to not hit. It’s not a huge deal because in most cases it goes away when the anesthesia wears off but it also sometimes take days/weeks and just simply shouldn’t happen if a dentist knows what they are doing. The entire side of my left face was 100% paralyzed for 12 hrs, even though I was numbed evenly. This is just a small example of not being trained well/correctly. Anyways, it’s been 3.5 weeks now since I got my teeth done. I have emailed DCT a few times regarding my discomfort and pain and know it hasn’t been long but the pain is now excruciating, unbearable and increasing everyday. I’ve seen 3 dentists/specialists here in the US and they have all told me the same thing. “My teeth look good but were not done correctly”. Essentially the way they changed my bite gave me TMJ (a super painful jaw issue) and my jaw/joints are not adjusting. I’ve been taking 6-10 ibuprofen a day just to function. I was super patient, hoping it was just gonna go away and have a high pain tolerance but it’s truly horrible. DCT has been responsive but my only option now is to fly back to turkey and spend thousands more on travel to have them HOPEFULLY* do it right this time. Which I’m not very confident in. This is the second baby we’ve had scanned at window to the womb Leeds. Our initial scan our baby was been uncooperative and wouldn’t show her face so after a very brief fetal check I was asked to wiggle around to get baby moving. After a few failed attempts to get her to move I tried to move the baby with my hands by jiggling my stomach and was very curtly told to “stop doing that” by the sonographer. I know my baby and I know what makes her move. After he then failed to pick her up on the scan I was told to book a rescan. I was informed this would be the 4D part of the scan only,  which I expected to be around 5 minutes as the initial fetal check took less than a minute and the website stated what we paid for would last around 5-7 minutes including the well being checks. We attended the rescan today and after spending all day trying to keep baby awake and alert in order to see her face I expected so so much more than what we received. We were in with the same sonographer much to my dismay, and after managing to get a couple of images of her face he asked us if we had any questions and the appointment was over. I was absolutely gutted. Happy to see the baby’s face but completely flabbergasted that he had not kept the scan on her face for more than a couple of seconds only to get a picture. Our first daughter that was scanned here, we watched her move around for a couple of minutes and watched her smile and yawn. I expected longer than a couple of seconds in order to tick a check box that we’d seen the baby. And again I left feeling deflated and like the £85 for the appointment and the two two hour round trips had been wasted. The only positive was the assistant in the room who tried to lighten the mood with pleasant commentary. My husband and I didn’t even feel comfortable enough to engage with one another in the room in front of the sonographer. Our last scan we received a video of the entire scan, which we didn’t this time as there was nothing to see or show. I will not be recommending window to the womb as I previously have to pregnant friends or booking further with them for friends or as gifts.

There is no regulation on how much vets can charge, so this whole industry is a very greedy free-for-all, especially the out of hours services.  Cynical too.  The welfare of animals is clearly not the reason companies like this exist.  It's a cold, hard money making machine whose target audience is captive one.  'Do you love your animal enough to find the money?'In fact, I had to weigh up not going vs. the potential risks to my cat on my recent visit (20.12.24) when I found out that VetsNow charge over £300 just for the visit with nothing else factored in. My diabetic cat was showing symptoms of Keto acidosis. I had to think about watching him all night and taking him to my vet first thing the next morning if he made it through, or only using this service if he suddenly collapsed.  But if it was keto, downhill could come too fast for help. Therefore, between a rock and a hard place, I took him, but decided that all I wanted from them was to rule out keto with a simple blood test.  No extras.  No preying on my love and concern for my boy.  You pay a platinum price but at 10-10.30 at night with only one couple in front of me whose dog was being seen by a vet, George wasn't seen for a long @45 minutes.  Nobody came to see me to update me.  I could have asked, but I really thought the vet I had seen with the dog was the only one there that night and I would just have to wait. George eventually saw a different vet to the vet seeing the dog.  I saw no-one else leaving (customers leave the same way).The initial intelligence gathering is done with your pet, but then George was taken away and I didn't see him again until we left at gone 1 a.m.  Yes, nearly 3 hours after what could only have been a simple blood test - heaven knows what they would have done if they'd had more pets there than just the two. Nothing else was said to me about any other investigations they did, so I can only assume he didn't have any.   I saw the vet once during the couple of hours they had him to tell me that the results of the blood test were imminent and then she disappeared again.  It wasn't exactly a well-oiled machine.  I understand from another professional that George's status could have been determined by a simple prick test - you know, a 2-minute job as opposed to a 3 hour sit-in.  George was really ill, so making him wait if there wasn't a good reason wasn't exactly putting his welfare first.When the vet first spoke to me, she said that George should stay in.  I said no.  One step at a time.  I just wanted him to be treated if he had keto.  The couple with the dog had been told the same and their treatment was going to cost £1,670-something.  This would be taken before the dog was admitted but the bill could be reduced if some of the projected treatment wasn't necessary.  They did not have this money and the woman had to call her father to come and use his card to pay for it, which he did.The vet stressed to me again when she gave me the results of the blood test that George should stay in so they could keep an eye on him.  I said no.  I don't like George being out of my sight unless it was essential.  He didn't have keto?  She said no, but they could only test him for four sorts of keto and there were others they couldn't test him for.  Therefore, they should keep an eye on him.  I said I would watch over him all night.  He hadn't got four sorts of keto, so that had to be promising. . . He was finally brought to the front desk after about another 20 minutes.The cost was £533 (+£25 for them to complete their bit of my insurance claim).  My small contribution towards their multi-million pound profits (check out Vets Now filings on the Companies House website).  We need competition from more caring companies AND FAST with handsome profits still to be made.  This service is little better than no service at all for what must be a large number of people who haven't got access to the huge amounts of money they demand and animals must be suffering.  I would pay a lot for George, but what they charge (and other similar outfits) isn't with his welfare in mind as the primary concern and I do resent that.

However, communication was non existent during her journey (she had a night over in Spain before flying on to Colombia) and when she arrived in Bogota she was left in her travel crate over night without being allowed out to go to the toilet and from what we could see when we collected her, with no food or water. It then took us 5 hours to get her out of the airport the next day due to a very inefficient Colombian process, during which time our dog remained in her travel crate and became very distressed. It was my understanding that the service we were paying for would cover the moment she was collected from me until the moment my husband collected her at the other end. Be warned that this is not the case. Once your pet leaves England, you will not hear from Airpets at all and it appears they do not maintain responsibility for them. When I looked back through all the communication we had received from airpets, in the first email they sent my husband with a quote, they recommended arranging a Colombian agent to help speed along the process at the airport here but this was never mentioned again once we had engaged their services and I would have expected our travel agent to offer to help with this, especially if it was important to guaranteeing our dogs well being during the journey. Overall we were very disappointed with the service received and would not recommend them.

We recently had a trip to Rome and was majorly let down by Tui.Our holiday started by being WhatsApp messaged to say they offer a service for free with our package to ask for advise and to help book tickets. We used this service to ask about trains… having arrived in Rome these has been cancelled since 1st November (we flew out 30th, and asked approx 28th Nov). After texting Tui we did get a quick response however all of their suggestion to get out of the airport were no good. The replacement bus was not taking more passengers, Uber wasn’t doing lift etc. After 2 hours of running around the airport we managed to get a local taxi (a lot more expensive than the train we’d planned and they even took us to the wrong hotel whilst following TUI’s address they provided) Once we arrived at the right hotel we then waited over 40mins to get in. They was key pads on the door to get in but we was not provided with a code. Reading reviews other providers provide guests with this. We tried ringing bells, calling numbers on the door to no luck. Fortunately another guest walked in which we then convinced them to let us in to try and find a reception.We then got to our room and headed out quickly due to the delays and was very hungry. Arriving back to our room we saw that our ‘Standard double bedroom’ was in fact a very uncomfortable sofa bed and the room was not as described by Tui. Our room was also next to a coffee bar which was constantly used by guests from 7am onwards. We also had construction works next door which we was not informed about. The construction work was that loud my partner could identify the tools being used by sound. Not to mention we could hear other guests enjoying themselves without the smart Tv as advertised and only channels in Italian to drown noise out. When arriving back from dinner one night we again couldn’t get into the hotel lobby… there was a power cut. Tui claim the power cut was 10mins however we banged on the door for approx 10mins when we was then let in by an American couple who confirmed the power has been out for awhile. We then scramble around in the dark to try and find a phone number for help. We then managed to get through where we have to try and explain what’s happening to someone in Italian which was approx another 10mins. We have a further 5min call and they arrive just over 10mins after this to fix the problem…. Definitely not the 10min outage Tui advise. And not a relaxing trip at all!It is at this point we complain as it just seems one issue after another, not to mention we’re not sure if the power will go out again. Tui email us the following day without useful help. By the time we get back the following day reception is closed. We continue to speak with Tui on this matter who only offer an update to descriptions on their website (which doesn’t help us as we were misled and miss-sold our room, not to mention the star rating difference too) as well as a £50 holiday voucher… as if I would want to spend yet more of our money with them. We feel insulted by this offer and still believe Tui need to do more. They have refused to refund us any money and said a voucher is ‘consistent with what the offer other people’ yet another member of staff confirmed it’s done on an individual basis. I asked for a refund rather than voucher which was denied. Again, why would I want to have another holiday and spend more money with them?

Returned from a 2 week trip to Vietnam with Audley a few weeks ago. Only now can I write about the trip with neutrality. Nothing to do with Vietnam which is an interesting country with friendly people. The problems were all to do with the very poor service we received from Audley. We were repeat customers and have traveled widely with a variety of operators. never before have we experienced the number or scale of issues we had on this trip. Things began to go downhill reading our 'final' itinerary and noticing that instead of a short flight from one place to another, we were due to fly to Ho Chi Mihn City at 6am then be driven for what turned out to be 4 hrs. On enquiry we were told the original flight was cancelled some weeks previously and this was the best alternative. We didn't see it that way - Audley state that they will keep people updated of any flight change as soon as they are aware, and that all arrangements are 'bespoke' ie arranged to best suit the customer. We consider that we should have been informed and consulted about how to deal with the cancelled flight immediately it happened. Eventually Audley agreed to change our flight to a later one (which meant they had to pay for an upgrade because it had virtually sold out by then - something they seemed to 'hold against' us as it was mentioned many times) Sadly no one in Vietnam knew of the change and we had to communicate with the UK many times before the new flight was confirmed - the day before it took place, 7 days into the trip. We further experienced being informed by the Audley app that we had landed from a different internal flight several hours before the flight took off - because the app was incorrect. We also were given incorrect information about booking in to the International flights by personal e-mail, and the information about booking in arrangements in the itinerary were not appropriate to the e-ticket arrangements that now exist for all flights. Most of the hotels that were booked for us were good, except one which was not suited to our needs ( I have mobility issues and the hotel supplies cycles-which I cant even get on- to get around) Furthermore it took 5 hours after arriving at this hotel (which we had been assured was one of the best Audley work with) to get a room with working air-con and the trouble we had during this time resembles a farce ! We went to this hotel to visit a floating market, which we anticipated would be a highlight of our trip (I am a keen photographer) In the Audley website the market is described as 'the throng of boats make it difficult to see the water' and 'boats are filed with teetering piles of fruit and vegetables' Many friends have seen such sights in the past but sadly it is not like that now - there are a few big black container boats from Cambodia with produce, but the trading is done elsewhere - surely Audley who claim to have very good, up to date local knowledge should know this ? The whole experience was beyond disappointing. We also found other descriptions to be inaccurate and misleading for example - Can Tho is not a small town, it is the 4 biggest City in Vietnam with well over 1 million inhabitants, Hoi An Old Town is lovely but it no longer has the Japanese bridge described and depicted on the website. The area is surrounded by unmentioned huge hotels and a 'party Island' on the opposite riverbank. The final major issue we had was with a guide who acted inappropriately. Having mentioned we were unhappy to Audley they started a process where the guide was informed he would not be continuing with us while we were on a long car journey with him - something we had expressly asked not to happen. The whole situation was very awkward, with the guide asking me twice if he had offended me and even trying to contact me when we got home. We understand why he would be upset but strongly feel it is for his employers to deal with updating him about expected attitudes. This is far from Audleys promise to offer 'the best guides' - we have to say the others were excellent. There were other 'niggles' along the way and we ended the holiday more stressed than we began, partly because as problems multiplied and escalated we worried about what might go wrong next rather than relax and feel looked after - surely the main reason that people pay a lot of money to a company like Audley.Why have I given a score of 2 ? On return it would have been zero ! We put together a full complaint -not that Audley give an indication that they have a complaint procedure or a customer services department on their website. We wanted to alert them to the flaws in their promotional material and help prevent future issues. We also wanted compensation. We believe this has been taken seriously, we have received apologies and we have agreed a sum. It wont give us the happy memories we hoped to bring back.

I've thought for a really long time about whether I should write this review - Kirsten is really lovely and professional and it does seem like this therapy works for many people and was very highly recommended from my GP and also other places, so I don't want to discourage others from taking an amazing opportunity to change. However I think it might be useful to hear an example of it not working as well as it could have done. I first went to Kirsten as my second child was due and I have a mortal fear of needles and medical procedures. I ended up having two sessions which were a lot of money for me but I felt that it would be worth it if it worked. There was a hypnosis element to the therapy, however I suspect I may just be someone who doesn't go into that state very easily. The other part of the therapy was more like CBT - and it was all really great stuff that was helpful, and I fully understood that it was about getting myself into a much healthier way of thinking. I think that because my problems come from quite a cerebral place anyway this is just not something I can think myself out of. At the start Kirsten did ask me if I thought I was unhelpable and I answered that I felt that if this didn't work nothing would. I guess the problem might have been that I didn't believe the problem could be fixed but I can't say that for sure.I've wanted to wait until plenty of time went past to assess the results (my son is now nearly a year old) but I'd say the only difference I experience when having to have a blood test or something like that is that now instead of becoming defensive and angry in response to what I perceived as a threat I am sobbing in shame at my own cowardice, as I did through my son's entire medical delivery.I've also felt a bit like something is wrong with me because of all the other reviews on here saying it worked for them - of course this is not something I blame the Therapy Lounge for - it just means that they are doing their job well! However I thought some people might be grateful for a different perspective on how it can go.

I'm really disappointed in Ci Food. I've only recently found out that they don't produce their own dog food, they just buy it from a bigger company, put their own label on the package and sell it to us as if they have produced it themselves. If you don't believe me, you can copy the ingredients of whatever Ci Food you're feeding your dog and paste it to Google. Then you will see that the exact same kibble / wet food with the exact same recipe is sold by other brands as well. For example, I was feeding my dog Tickety Boo Large Breed Puppy (Salmon, Sweet Potato & Vegetables) and Top Drawer Puppy Chicken & Rice. If you copy the ingredients of Tickety Boo Large Breed Puppy and paste it to Google, you will see that the exact same kibble with the exact same recipe is also sold under different names by brands like Furlington, Country Kibble, Challenge Dog Food, Dog's Life Dog Food, Canine Kitchen, Luv Dogz, etc. etc. - brands I've never even heard of before. And the list goes on. Obviously they all buy the same kibble from the same big company, put their own labels and prices on it, and sell it as if they've produced it themselves. Similarly when I've copied and pasted the ingredients of Top Drawer Puppy Chicken & Rice, again I've seen that the exact same wet food with the exact same recipe is also sold under different names by brands like Pets Love Europa, PawPrints, Lovejoys, etc. I recommend you google the ingredients of whatever you are feeding your dog as well. When these companies tell us things like 'we have developed this recipe' or 'we have added this and that to this kibble', they are lying to us because they have never produced the kibble themselves in the first place. They simply buy and sell it and only care about the profit they make.

I bought a rather expensive Bosch battery just over 3 years ago as it had a good warranty. Tayna delivered it the next day. I had the electrics checked out and bought a second hand battery from a scrap yard. This second hand battery didn't fail me and still hasn't. I performed all of the home tests with the Bosch battery as Tayna suggested (including removing it from the car and trickle charging it). It worked for a day and then failed again. Tayna wanted me to return it. This cost £20, no fault was found and it was returned to me.A week later I installed the Bosch battery. It started my 2009 diesel s-max straight away. I took it for a 40 minute drive, parked for 10 minutes and came home. It started OK again.The next day I did a 10 minute journey. I was parked for 5 minutes (getting diesel) and the car started, but struggled to turn over. I drove home in 10 minutes and left the car until the next morning.The next day it would not start at all. I used a jump pack and it started. I did an hour journey and parked for the day. When I went to start the car, I needed to use my jump pack again.I took the battery out and put in the second hand battery back in. I had no more problems starting ever since. I invested in another charger and trickle charged the Bosch battery. It did the same as before, worked for a couple of times and died... Back went in the second hand battery with no problems.I am now at a loss. I have already spent £20 for you to say that the battery is fine.I'll use a local motor factors in future.

Just an observation I made with the Wise Visa Debit Card (which is "temporarily" unavailable in the US), but it will not work on some sites that require 3D Secure transactions, which is mandatory in Japan starting at the end of January 2025.For example, I wasn't able to add my Wise Visa Debit Card to JR East's Online Train Reservation website, which is important if you want to book train tickets from Narita Airport to Tokyo.Additionally, some ATMs in Japan will not accept Wise Debit Cards, regardless if they are on the MasterCard or Visa payment networks.And finally, there is a limit to how much you can withdraw at ATMs without incurring additional fees. Once you go above that limit, you have to start paying fees, which will diminish the value of your withdrawals.Overall, with US customers being locked out from debit cards, as well as some merchants and train reservation websites in Japan not working well with Wise Debit cards, I do not recommend this service when traveling to Japan. I wouldn't even recommend this service for any ATM withdrawal in light of the Evolve Bank and "Trust" data breach earlier in 2024.

DD is the parent company of medfx. My name is Mikaiel. I am a medical student and a locum pharmacy dispenser, balancing these roles as the main breadwinner for my household while managing the heavy demands of medical school. What drew me to these shifts was the higher rate, which would just about cover the cost of my commute from London—a two-hour journey each way involving the Jubilee line to Stratford and then Greater Anglia to Witham. Before committing, I asked my agency to confirm the payment schedule and was assured that MedFx operated on a weekly payment basis. Under this understanding, I accepted two additional shifts for the following week, on the 16th and 17th of October.Although I encountered significant challenges during my commute, including a Jubilee line shutdown at North Greenwich and Greater Anglia train delays caused by a first aid incident, I ensured that my working hours were always accurately reflected. Any late arrivals were promptly communicated to the store manager and other senior staff, and I adjusted my break times to account for the delays. All of these details were documented in my invoices, which were verbally confirmed by the store manager, Farah, and another senior staff member during her absence.Payment IssuesDespite completing all four shifts and submitting accurate invoices, I have yet to receive payment six weeks later. MedFx’s process for verifying bank details—requiring a phone call before processing invoices—has not been followed. I have yet to receive this phone call, despite providing my details multiple times via email, text, and over the phone.Last week, on Friday, 15th November, I was informed by my agency that I could expect my payment that day. With urgent bills to cover, I stayed up until 01:30 to check my account, only to find no payment had been made. When I contacted my agency that evening, they claimed that this was their mistake and that Farah had only said she was “trying” to have the payment sorted for Friday. This vague and unhelpful explanation only added to my frustration.Inadequate CompensationOn Monday, 18th November, my agency informed me that MedFx had added 2.5 hours to my invoice for the 9th October shift as compensation for the delay. While I appreciate the gesture, it falls far short of addressing the financial stress caused by this situation. I’ve had to withdraw cash from a credit card to cover essential expenses, incurring fees that exceed the compensation offered. MedFx’s delays and lack of accountability have caused unnecessary hardship and stress, and their response is deeply inadequate.ConclusionAt this point, my patience has run out. This entire experience has been exhausting, and MedFx has demonstrated an alarming disregard for their workers. Their lack of urgency, poor communication, and failure to meet their obligations exemplify how companies can neglect independent workers by hiding behind broken systems.I strongly recommend avoiding MedFx. If this is how they treat their employees, I can only imagine how poorly they treat their customers. For full details of my experience, as well as photos of our correspondence, email me or visit the pharmacy review section of my website, gapyearmbbs.com.To MedFx: If you are reading this, I invite you to provide a response.

At the time the course was created, the strategy wasn't bad for the current markets at that time, but has since become much less effective. I have moved on to other avenues and since been able to easily pass evals and become a $200,000 funded prop firm trader. Learning to trade is the hardest thing you'll ever do, and it is the most difficult occupation out there. G7 is a good place to start for a new trader, but it won't be the last stop in your journey to success. Finally, for those of you that are serious, trading is 90% psychology. Success is found in the mind game.

After reading so many of the reviews on here, I can tell that a lot of it is advertisement for other (probably scammy services) and identify problems with this company that I myself have not faced. I took a gamble with the first deposit of roughly $27. Waited a day and tested a withdrawal. It worked so whoever mentions high deposits before you can get withdrawals, that has not been the case with me at all. I was able to withdraw the day after my first small deposit. Also one thing to note about withdrawals are the transfer fees. HashFactor makes the fee structure for each supported crypto very transparent on the withdrawal screen. Another thing worth noting is that low amount withdrawals (like $10-20) are a waste of money. Say you have $15 in your mining earnings, you need to account roughly $9-10 received after fees so for those low amounts you’re essentially wasting $5 each time which adds up if you do it often enough. My suggestion is to let it sit for a week before withdrawing. As far as withdrawals go, they make it seem like you can make 24/7 withdrawals (or maybe I understood their verbiage incorrectly) but in my case it’s one withdrawal per 24 hours. As far as constructive criticism goes, I do think that should be clarified better in the FAQs on the website.Any withdrawal I have made has arrived in my wallet within 20 minutes. It’s reasonable to expect it to take longer if the network is congested so don’t get discouraged if it takes longer. I simply keep track of my wallet number on MemPool and once I see the pending transfer, I just give it the time to confirm on the blockchain. It’s always came through. Another note is about their mining estimates. Once you purchase more speed, your mining estimates will change based on that. Given the volatility of crypto, expect those mining estimates to change as time goes on. Mine goes up some days, on others it goes down. Either way, the daily estimates have thus far been mostly accurate. I’d read reviews of others depositing but not getting their speed. That is one thing that really made me nervous at first. There’s a wallet to deposit to but what is that wallet and how does it ensure that my payment goes to the right account? Well, the answer is simple really. I have surmised that it is your own custom deposit wallet. So whatever you send to that wallet address will automatically post to your HashFactor account once it is confirmed on the blockchain. I’ve made roughly 4 different deposits totaling around $250 and each time I’ve gotten the speed I paid for using the wallet address they’ve given me within moments of confirming on the blockchain. So far the whole process has been fairly smooth. Like with all new crypto ventures I discover, I remain cautiously optimistic and begin with low investments until the company fully earns my trust. I’d like for this site to stick around for a while. There is real potential here. The best part about this site is that they make it so easy to understand everything (from my perspective) that you don’t have to know much about mining to know how much you’ll be making off of your investments. The hardest part is really learning about crypto wallets, transfer fees and all that jazz. If you know how to operate a crypto wallet, send/receive funds and can navigate a website, you can totally do HashFactor. Since this is a relatively new company, I advise being cautious about how much you invest. Don’t invest what you can’t afford to lose. It is tempting to drop your life savings into it but wait for the company to prove its longevity before making any huge deposits. I plan on investing more into HashFactor once I receive my full RoI. Since I am still new to all of this, I will report back in a few weeks with my thoughts up to that point. So far it seems very promising and has delivered on its promises so far but based on other reviewers on here it does make me skeptical about the long-term.

I have been a member for 40 years starting off with a trailer tent and progressing via caravans to motorhomes as my wife and I retired. The aspect that caused me to first reconsider renewing my membership was the fact that when the sites re-opened after Covid no extension of membership was given to compensate for the period when the sites were closed. The direction of the club has changed radically in recent years with a move away from general caravanning to a form of glamping. Paradoxically over the same period our motorhome had become more sophisticated and our site requirements have reduced. In previous years I have purchased insurance through the club and travelled with Red Pennant, however recovery is included in my insurance with Comfort. I have previously booked ferry crossings with the club, but found that changing the booking was expensive and unwieldy being limited to Monday to Friday office hours. I now book direct with the operator. As a motorhome user our usage of the sites has changed, arriving at say 16:00 and leaving at 10:00 the next morning which makes site fees approaching £40 for two adults very expensive for the time spent on site. When we first joined the alternatives were poor or non existent. However in the intervening years commercial sites are now both of an equal quality and competitive, many local councils, as well as Forestry Scotland allow parking one night in seven on a no frills basis at minimal cost. For us continued membership is too hard to justify and consequently we will not be renewing. Coincidentally we are also members of the CCC and have renewed our membership which perhaps tells its own story.
