AVOID Petmedics (Worsley). They're a cold-hearted conveyer-belt money-driven business, totally lacking any genuine care for animals. Our pet dog was happily running around playing with a large twig when it suddenly began choking and fighting for its life. The twig had broken up and part had gone down the back of its throat obstructing it. I desperately tried to remove it by inserting my fingers and in my panicked efforts believed that I may have pushed it or part of it further down its windpipe. We rushed to Petmedics (Worsley) hoping to have its throat examined and requested  sedation and endoscopy to do a deep examination to check if anything was stuck down its windpipe.. This frightening experience - for us and our pet - was shockingly not treated as an 'emergency' and zero 'urgency' was shown. Our dog was placed in a room for three hours without any treatment or examination. After waiting this long we was finally introduced to the vet, who admitted the dog had just then resisted her attempt at examining its throat, to which we reiterated that we wanted it sedated and endoscopy carried out to ensure there wasn't any blockage further down its windpipe. She dismissed it and casually said to take it home and if it started choking again to bring it back. We insisted that she examine its throat by endoscopy, but she replied that if she did, it'd be the following day. Thereby, placing our dog at risk. After a futile plea that fell on deaf ears, we went to reception where we was billed approximately £185 for consultation and treatment. I argued that the vet openly admitted that she had not properly examined or treated our dog and had refused to do any procedures that night, yet, we was billed regardless. I was adamant that I wasn't paying this outrageous amount, just for our dog to wait in a room for three hours. To emphasise, it was the vet who had billed us, not the receptionist. So she was fully aware she was demanding payment for none-existent work. My threat of walking out the door without paying a single penny, persuaded her to accept only the £85 consultation charge. This experience was very disturbing, I can liken it to a baby almost choking to death on an object or swallowing a toy, rushing it to A & E only for the nurses to refuse to examine its throat/air-ways for any obstruction and saying take it home and if it starts choking, to bring it back. Then demanding an extortionate payment for work not done. This company and the particular vet involved has destroyed any faith I had in vets being in the job for animal welfare, clearly some are motivated by career/financial reasons. I actually regret paying the £85 consultation fee, because the vet didn't earn nor deserve it. I am angry and disgusted more than can be imagined at the callous indifference this vets displayed towards our pet dog in a time of 'emergency'.

Start of Enquiry October, 2022We wanted to book two cruises and spoke with “the sales girl” on this matter.  The first was a cruise around South America and the second a cruise around the Far East.  Our first cruise started in March 2023 and the second had to be delayed until February 2024 as the one we wanted was booked up till then.We asked the sales girl for luxury hotels and business class flights as we were going to do this in style, the initial email exchange was even headed “Luxury”.Lisa booked us in to a hotel in Buenos Aries and Santiago (we were going to stay a few days in each city either end of the cruise) respectively for the first cruise.  The sales girl also advised that BA’s premium Economy was a far better and cheaper solution for the flights rather than go to the expense of Business Class.The second cruise was slightly opaquer as, it was further in the future and the hotels and flights were to be left until nearer the time and Cruise2 would arrange these.  Cruise2 insisted that to hold the prices we had to agree a figure for both holidays but did mention that for the second cruise there was more than enough cash in the budget for good flights and luxury hotels.About three weeks before the first holiday (South America) we had a look at the hotels which had been recommended and were really surprised to find that one of the hotels which had been chosen was still pretty devastated after the riots which had gone on in Buenos Aries a few months earlier.  Trip Adviser said best avoided, so we got back in touch with Cruise2 and asked this hotel be changed.  Cruise2 said we had to chose a different hotel ourselves and they would arrange the change.  So much for customer service! But onto the real issue, the second cruise.  Cruise2 advised us they had chosen Qatar Airways for our flights and two hotels for each end of the holiday.  The flights in themselves seemed okay but Cruise2 had recommended and purchased Economy seats for our outward and inward journeys.We contacted Cruise2 three times to discuss the choice of seats and they said “Qatar economy seats are as good, if not better, than BA Premium Economy” so I did some research and could find nothing to support that statement. But they said you’ll save money on business class which we clearly would.  Equally, by this time we were so close to the holiday to buy Business Class seats would cost a lot more.  The first flight took around 6/7 hours and the second 9 hours.  Believe me when I say the Economy seats chosen were just that - economy.  The first flight was very uncomfortable but the second of 9 hours starting 1am in the morning was just sheer torture.These economy seats on Qatar didn’t even come close to Premium.  I cannot complain to Qatar as we got exactly what was asked for by Cruise2.  When we arrived in Singapore (after 9 hours) our thoughts were we have to do this all again and I was not looking forward to it.We arrived at our hotel and were allocated our room.  We just wanted to have a shower, and get out and explore.  But, the tap on the bathroom sink was hanging off.  We had a shower, the bath would not drain, splashing around in foul water! The safe would not work.  The chair in the room was falling to bits.We complained to the hotel and were given another room. A luxury hotel chosen by Cruise2!We looked at Cruise2 complaints on their website and it said do not wait until the end of your holiday to complain, do so as soon as you notice something wrong.We did, guess what happened, NOTHING. Just long periods of no reply and prevarication.The cruise ended in Hong Kong and the only thing Cruise2 offered us was to upgrade our return flights for an additional £1,100.00 each at our expense.That was it.However, I did manage to upgrade our first flight home (the 9 hour flight) which was a joy. I certainly was not giving Cruise2 more money booked these directly.  The second flight was back to economy and with all the attendant discomforts.To summarize, Cruise2 took our money and booked us cheap flights and hotels.  Clearly they wanted to maximize their profits, and then when things got difficult because they did not follow our request at the outset they just left us high and dry, despite us complaining at the start of the holiday as per their guidelines.  Cruise2 took our money, gave us promises and then failed to meet them.We have several more cruises to do and we will never use this bunch again.I would advise all customers to be very wary of this company.  If things do go wrong you are on your own.  And just an update, despite Cruise2 sending us an email advising they were looking into the matter at more or less the start of the holiday we have heard nothing from them and that’s twenty one days after the end date of our holiday.I would think very carefully before using this bunch, we will never use them again.They offered £40.00 to remove!

The water pump was horrendously noisy every time you ran a tap so washing your hands through the night was a no no incase you woke the house. The back door did not lock properly according to the brief instructions. To be clear, nobody from Guestready seemed to understand ths the keys only working in ONE back door, which was the one you close first, before the main door beside could be closed...for which the keys provided did NOT fit into the lock. The reply to this review again doesn't seem to understand this. It shouldn't take more than 2 minutes to work out how to lock a door, so we had to carry our valuables with us for the stay. The mugs and plates were chipped, so there wasn't enough mugs for the 7 of us at one time. The cooker was in Czech so we couldn't use it, one of the windows was so dirty, I were embarrassed we persuaded our family to stay with us so we took that room and gave them the bigger room. There was no dining table, just a coffee table with dining chairs around, out of date food left in the cupboard, nappies in the bins outside which stank whenever you opened it to put rubbish in, and a hoard of cigarette butts in the back garden which we had to clean up. Constructively, I think there should be a welcome pack which would help paying customers on things like explaining how to use the cooker given there was no manual available (the communications received from Guestready were not correct to the type of cooker in place so we just used the hob), useful local info for buses to city centre to save on expensive cabs places to eat, emergency numbers in the event it was needed...simple things that would have really helped us. The company were quick in response over issues until I pushed over the concern for the back door when the communications stopped. They did advise they would sort reimbursement once I had completed the check out. I'm disappointed however that since being given a reimbursement, I haven't been messaged to advise this. I only noticed when I checked the account. Feels like sour grapes. I think at the very least I should have got the cleaning fee reimbursed as this wasn't done very well. The best thing about the stay was the clean bathrooms. They were immaculate so can't fault that, but I have to be honest and say that was the best thing about it. Either the cleaning company are not telling the truth and doing Guestready a disservice or there genuinely isn't the care for ensuring the presentation and upkeep of the properties are in place by landlords. Its a shame that it put such a taint on a very sensitive trip. I won't ever have to book a trip like this again thankfully, however I certainly wouldn't recommend this property unless Guestready put some proper checks in place and improved it's current condition.

“When Chaos Meets Chainsaw Burgers: A Harvester Tale to Forget”Ah, Harvester, where memories of fresh salads and smiling staff go to die. My latest visit was the culinary equivalent of stepping on a LEGO barefoot—unnecessarily painful and oddly hilarious in hindsight.Let’s start with Jackie. Jackie was the embodiment of “customer service is optional.” Abrupt? Sure. Smiling? Absolutely not. Watching her sigh as if grabbing a vinegar bottle required the strength of a thousand warriors was truly a spectacle. Then, in a masterclass of efficiency, she placed our empty vinegar bottle on a table being prepared. Why bother with such herculean tasks like replacing an empty bottle with one that had actual vinegar?We attempted to order calamari. “None in, been the same for weeks,” she quipped, as though calamari were some mythical creature no longer caught in these parts. Onto the refit: whoever designed this place clearly had a sense of humor. Salad sauces and bread rolls were placed in the busiest staff thoroughfare, a corridor of chaos where staff and plates collided like bumper cars. One of these collisions involved my plate being knocked out of my hands by a poor server. Not their fault—the layout is more dangerous than a reality show obstacle course.Now, the food. Oh, the food. I ordered the Beef Classic Burger, which I can only assume was named ironically. Cutting it required either a chainsaw or a gym membership. It had all the flavor of damp cardboard, saved only by the bacon and cheese desperately trying to salvage its reputation. The chips tasted like they’d been fried in the tears of previous customers—hinting strongly at oil that probably pre-dates the refit.And the famous salad bar? Once a Harvester highlight, now reduced to a sad collection of not olives and empty condiment bottles. One sauce took 25 minutes to replenish after multiple requests. Were they making it from scratch? Milking cows for the dressing? Who knows.When I raised my concerns about the inedible burger, the kind lady who seated us was apologetic, understanding, and shocked that Jackie hadn’t checked in with us. She issued a refund, proving that someone here still had a pulse and a sense of decency.But the grand finale? Waiting ages to pay at the bar because no one seemed to notice we still existed.Dear Harvester, your refit is a masterpiece of poor planning, your staff (excluding one gem) seem to be in the running for the “Least Interested Employee” awards, and your food? Let’s just say I won’t be needing a burger-flavored chainsaw any time soon.If you’re looking for a dining experience that’s part sitcom, part disaster movie, and entirely forgettable, Harvester’s got you covered.

I wasnt given a great deal of confidence about the transplant as each nurse was asking me if i had knocked my head? I had two large bloody spots on my head which they werent able to identify. Later on it would seem that those parts are fairly 'bald' I am somewhat satisfied with the results, although I still have to use a hair thickener to fill it out.Upon reflection you get what you pay for. When totalling up the flight costs and the underwhelming experience I will be getting the last bit done in the uk. We really do have no recourse or ability to question what has been done. This was intended to be the trip of a lifetime - our retirement reward to a place I'd always wanted to go to, The Amalfi Coast.  We are not confident travellers and based on Trustpilot Reviews and Audley's website we felt safe trusting our trip to them and paying a premium price.  At no point did they admit to us that once we got to Italy, we would be dealing with third parties - mostly Tui and not Audley.  We would not have booked if we had known.  We booked our own flights to Naples and had the most horrendous time with threatened cancellation and a 3 hour delay.  We phoned the Duty Agent to ensure that our transfer was made aware of our circumstances.  The Duty Agent was rather off hand and said we should have called Italy direct but agreed to notify the company organising the transfer on our behalf as we were being rushed to boarding to ensure the plane could leave and land before midnight in Naples.  On arrival, weary and exhausted, we could not find our transfer.  Travellers who had paid far less and travelled with Tui were all collected.  There was no message on my phone, nothing.  We were left in Naples airport at the mercy of the touts.  We eventually got through to the ground agent, Citalia, who told us the transfer had been and gone and they couldn't find another.  When asked what we should do, they said, get a taxi and couldn't tell us what a fair price was - negotiate they said.  It was now past midnight, we were exhausted and had no option but to join a long queue where we were pestered by touts and taxi drivers who were trying to double book people to fill their seats.  We were lucky.  We were not ripped off and arrived safely at our hotel.  No thanks to Audley.  In the morning an email arrived from the duty officer telling me they hadn't been able to arrange an alternative transfer and to get a refund from the airline!  This was not an auspicious start.  Naples was a great experience, lovely hotel, excellent guide and the driver arrived on time to take us to Sorrento.  Unfortunately, the hotel in which were to spend the next 6 nights was not up to scratch.  Italy was unseasonably cold and windy and our hotel was only suitable to hot sunshine - the name Helios, says it all.  Its breakfast gazebo was freezing and windblown and the electricity failed for the hot food and toast.  The manageress was curt and mercenary when we asked for a bottle of water in the room and as for tea/coffee making facilities forget it.  There was only a tiny bar area inside - everything was outside but it was too cold to use, condemning us to our rooms which were not designed to be used that way.  The space was on the terrace, which was too cold to sit out on.  As the hotel didn't do evening food, you were always forced out to eat - a good 15 minute down the hill into town or pay £30 for a taxi!  There was no letter, as promised in the Audley booklet with all the details of your tours etc.  Both hotels looked blank when I asked for such a document.  This rather left us in the dark.   Questions we'd pre-asked and specific modifications, such as food we don't eat to not be served on one trip had clearly not been relayed thus particular experiences were not what we'd anticipated.  I want to make it clear that my lack of satisfaction is that our needs were not met and we had paid top dollar for this trip.  Audley apologised and offered us refunds for elements as well as helping us out with a last minute guide which they partially paid for.  However, they really didn't have the local knowledge they claimed - nothing was mentioned about the Easter parades which are famous in the region and which shut down the towns when they are on.  The agent had never heard of Paestum, which is World Heritage Site, when we asked to visit it as part of our itinerary, then left it off and had to be reminded.  Thus, we feel we paid for a 5 star experience and received a three star one instead.  We wouldn't use Audley again - they did not give us the bespoke experience we used them for.

I booked an apartment in Madeira well ahead of time, as I wanted a good location with sea view. I found one in Praia Reis Magos, Canico de Baixo.Reviews of the apartment were very good and the views over the ocean, terrific.As time passed, I checked reviews occasionally and read a few mentions of ants in the apartment. I was concerned about that and asked GuestReady if that issue was resolved. They assured me it was. ( I was misled- see later).We came to Madeira on 2nd Jan, and found the apartment to be spacious. Otherwise, it soon was apparent that GuestReady are anything but “ready” At least in our case.The apartment was worn or “tired” you might say , with scratched wooden floors, peeling paint on the balcony, fraying cushions. The kitchen had items missing ( only one wine glass, no bread knife , one set of towels and linen, one egg cup etc ) and some of what was there was broken or filthy ( spatter guard, bin, food strainer). Similarly the pillows we were expected to sleep on were stained yellow, the sealant around the bath badly stained etc. I could say more.Guestready did respond in supplying new pillows and the items missing ( eg new wine glasses), and were cheerful and apologetic.The first time we used the washing machine the kitchen flooded. The outlet hose had not been connected. I spent an hour mopping up and had to warn the occupier of the flat below of possible water seeping in, who said the same thing happened twice last year. She gave me an email address for our apartments actual owner.* Guestready attended about an hour later and quickly assessed the issue and fixed the hose.Despite all this, there was more. The ant problem had not been resolved at all. The place was infested with them. Guestready had put ant traps down and left sprays for us to use ( to kill them) which to my mind was not a resolution of the issue but a sticking plaster. Who wants to be spraying chemicals all over the place and then cleaning away dead ants?The ants were seen everywhere; bathroom, bedroom, kitchen, including cutlery drawer, and twice on my bedside table inside my drinking water cup. No food could be left out and even rubbish like kitchen waste I kept in the freezer until there was enough to take down to the bin store.I brought this to the attention of GuestReady each time and it brought no positive response other than “ are you using the spray?” . At around this time I attempted to negotiate a partial refund with GuestReady who didn’t respond in a positive manner.To cut a long story short, in exasperation I contacted Airbnb who looked at evidence I supplied (photos mostly) and upheld my complaint. I was able to move to a new apartment in Funchal and recover money that had been paid , but only for unused time at the first apartment, plus the cleaning fee. Guestready showed no interest in refunding money for the poor conditions we had endured, and suggested the filthy state under the beds had accumulated during our stay. Perhaps ours was an unusual occurrence where GuestReady are concerned. I hope that is the case. I wondered why so many reviews had been so positive and thought it may be that most people staying there would only be there a week or so, whereas we had booked two months so the issues would really grate over time. I don’t know. The pity is that it could be a really enjoyable place to stay. An updating ( refurbishing) of the flat, proper solution to the ant infestation ( which I discovered is not confined to the one apartment but affected several if not most in the block) and GuestReady doing their job properly ( doing an inventory of contents and checking for missing/broken items and condition of everything. Oh, and not misleading prospective guests.*who I emailed later to make aware of concerns. No response.

WARNING - If you are thinking of signing up for this course, there are a few things you need to SERIOUSLY CONSIDER!Note: I can only comment up to Foundation level Module 5.- The promotional Video would have you think you are signing up for a turnkey solution platform ... Similar to Etoro. You are not! It is only when you are into Module 4/5 that it becomes clear you will need to think about 3rd party platforms / Brokerage, etc. that come with their own monthly subscriptions. (You are ultimately only buying the training knowledge and some training applications/tools). - The promotional video states you get a 30 day money back guarantee, again beware, If you buy the course, you can complete Module 1, and still claim under the 30 day guarantee, BUT! soon as you start module 2, you forfeit your guarantee. Double check the terms, as this can change.- G7FX, don't tell you what hardware you require, i have a Chromebook laptop, and some of the training application/tools, pertinent to course are not compatible!.- Another issue that is not made clear until you have purchased the course is the time commitment required to become a competent G7FX trader... 6months....12months... depending on your experience. - Lastly, the promotional video shows you candle sticks populated with the number of buyers and sellers. The training course uses a different application (Sierra Charts).I take nothing away from G7FX, NV is very knowledgeable and the training is straight forward, but the platform he uses moves at cracker-jack speed and he keeps mentioning about AI bots being on the platform, he mentions that you will never keep up with them, as they spoof the market with false signals... That is when i started to get real doubts, and these training modules were created during Covid era,  and as we know, AI/Chap GPT, have all entered the scene, which is going to make it even more difficult trading for novices/intermediaries As said, NV knows his stuff, but you will need to be an experienced trader before considering this course.If you are an Etoro trader like me and you find the platform user friendly (Turnkey), then this course might not be for you.Good luck and for what it was worth, i did enjoy the early modules, it does give some insight to what you are up against...on any platform.

Got fertility bloods done at the start of October,  the results came back that I was perimenopausal. I've just turned 30 so this was quite a shock and very upsetting. According to hertility, my FSH was very high, AMH and oestrogen almost non-existent. After a few weeks crying and mulling over the results I contacted my own GP and a full blood count and hormone profile done. I've just got the results back from those and in the words of my GP "everything is perfect, everything is within range, nothing that would suggest perimenopause" . There was 20 days between the 2 blood tests.. of course different times of your cycle you would expect some slight increases/decreases but the difference in my results could have literally been for 2 different people. My dog was in the practice to receive his vaccination for the year. He also had an ear check and the vet found they were a little swollen so prescribed anti inflammatory medication ear drops. My dog was quite distressed when in the vet consultation room and the vet did not demonstrate to me how to put the ear drops in (if she would have done so I would have recognised that my dog would not have allowed me to put them in).Once I got home, I tried to administer and my dog became very distressed, would not allow me to administer. I persevered and kept trying for two days, tried two of us, tried a different person trying to administer but still he was quite distressed.I phoned Apex on the Saturday and asked if I could bring the ear drops back in exchange for another treatment. The nurse on the phone told me I should bring my dog in for a demonstration on how to put the ear drops in, I explained I did not require a demonstration as I knew how to administer, the problem was that my dog did not want me to administer them.I asked to simply swap for another alternative treatment. I explained he had just been seen by the vet. The nurse told me she could not offer this unless I brought my dog in and paid for a consultation and alternative treatment - I had just been in the practice two days prior and paid for treatment which if the vet would have tried to put in my dogs ear, she would have known my dog would not tolerate. Dissatisfied, I felt the practice were just trying to make money from me and felt very uneasy about the situation so put the phone down and went back to trying another method of putting my dogs ear drops in. Luckily, a distraction technique worked (for anyone struggling- try to administer whilst your dog is waiting at the door to go out for a walk/to the garden).My dog is seen nearly every two months to have his glands emptied, we are always straight on the phone to the vet if anything is wrong, we are probably on the phone to the vets a little too much! But want to make sure he is looked after as he is like our child! We would pay for anything he needed - but we felt we were being taken advantage of in this case.My faith was shattered in the practice from then on - at the beginning I thought I had found a genuinely great practice but unfortunately, the owner shattered it even more on the Monday following my phone call with the nurse.On Monday, I found an email in my inbox from the owner asking me to call him to speak about his concerns which the nurse had escalated to him. The owner had asked me to work with him to “better understand each other” and “take feedback”.So, I sent a very detailed email allowing him my feedback on what I though was handled wrongly, what I thought could have been said better, even giving my opinion on what the nurse could have said on the phone.I felt that the nurse was very condescending on the phone and let the owner know this on my emails. He let me know that he had worked with the nurse in question for over 11 years and he had never heard her being condescending over the phone. This may be the case, however, to basically make out like I am lying about her sounding condescending is very unprofessional and I really did not appreciate this from the owner.He let me know that if I had spoken with him on the Saturday, he would have waived the fee. However, the nurse never mentioned any of this on the phone.I ended my emails by asking why, if they had known and worked with one another for 11 years, had the nurse not offered to exchange my dogs ear drops for an alternative - waiving the fee?For asking this question, and offering my feedback - which the owner did ask for on several occasions - my dog was banned from the practice.In all my years of being a pet owner, in fact in all my years of dealing with ANY business at all I have NEVER experienced bad customer service like it.So, BEWARE, if you feel strongly about anything, or have an opinion… be careful you may be banned from the practice for sharing it.

Booking TY4FGUJVPArrived at the apartment to discover that the information provided for gaining entry, was completely non-sensical. The keys were supposed to be in a keybox, next to the apartment window. As the apartment was on the first floor, this seemed unlikely, but apparently the keybox was close to a bicycle and a flowerpot. After spending quite a while searching for such items, we drew a complete blank. After several calls to GuestReady we finally located the keybox attached to a guardrail by the side of the road, a significant distance from the property and with no bicycle or flowerpot in sight!On gaining entry, we had to navigate our way through a pitch black lobby to a lift whereupon pressing the button, the light went out and we were back in darkness. The lift didn't seem to be working and the immediate thought that we were now trapped in the lift, causing even more stress. Fortunately, we found out how to make the lift work, but ultimately discovered that this problem occurred every time we used the lift.We exited the lift, again in complete darkness, to be confronted with a door that could only be opened if the door was pulled towards one, whilst the key was being turned.We really didn't need all of that completely avoidable aggravation after travelling for fourteen hours!On settling into the apartment, we discovered there were absolutely no instructions on how to use any of the appliances supplied and several essential items of kitchen equipment were either missing or faulty.We also discovered that a significant part of the wall in the sitting area was badly damp and was covered with black, furry mould. The cooker and the fridge hadn't been cleaned properly and a corner of the balcony was filthy and full of rubbish.The following morning we awoke to find we had no water and that situation remained until lunchtime. On Monday morning, of the second week, we awoke to find we had no hot water and that situation remained for several days, meaning we had to take cold showers and I had to boil water in the kettle, in order to shave. Ultimately we were without hot water for more than half our stay.Finally, the lights in the lobby were fixed, but there were still no lights on our floor for several days afterwards.We called GuestReady numerous times throughout the visit, but couldn't get an answer most of the time and out of about ten emails we sent to them, we got no confirmation of when the problems would be fixed, apart from a reply, promising to fix all of the problems AFTER our departure; a lot of use that was to us!GuestReady didn't address any of the problems, save advising us to buy replacements for the missing kitchen essentials, for which they would reimburse us, but that really shouldn't be the responsibility of the guest. I don't know whether the lights and hot water were eventually fixed as a result of their intervention, as we got no tangible response whatsoever about those problems.The apartment itself is spacious,very well laid-out and well designed. It would warrant five stars if it hadn't been for all the problems, but unfortunately they seriously tainted our stay.We have rented apartments in Marseille about a dozen times over the last nine years, with few problems, but this was the worst experience by far and we will never use GuestReady again.Since I posted this review, GuestReady have agreed to refund 30% of the rental fee, which is great, so I have added an extra star to the review and would now consider using them again but nonetheless, that doesn't alter the negative effect all of the problems had on our holiday.
